base_record_snapshot.lesson: When one lane chains a sub-step, the sub-step must not resolve the tic from a DIFFERENT authority than its parent — or the chain silently consumes stale state forever. Lived at tic 680: harmony-invoke.sh chains braid-invoke.sh, but the two input builders resolve the tic from different sources. harmony-input-builder.py reads conformation tic_count_physical; braid-input-builder.py (line ~130) reads the ECONOMY current-pointer as PRIMARY authority, with conformation only as an absent-pointer FALLBACK. Because the cadence cycle order runs harmony_invoke (position 3) before economy_heartbeat (position 10), the economy pointer has not yet advanced when braid reads it — so braid resolves tic N-1 on EVERY cadence run. Verified structurally, not inferred: the mtime diagonal shows braid writing tic N-1 in the same session economy writes tic N, consistently across tics 677/678/679/680; and at cycle end the economy pointer reads 680 while the braid pointer still reads 679. Consequence: harmony's tic-680 derived stance ('name-the-boundary-before-the-point-of-no-return', regime 'breaking', cable_tension 0.867) was computed from tic-679 braid state, and no braid-tic-680 packet exists until the next run. The defect is NOT that a tic is missing — it is that tic resolution is INCONSISTENT ACROSS AXES inside a single chain, the same shape tic 679 found in _collect_targets. The generalizable rule: a chained sub-step inherits its parent's clock, or it declares its own clock as a first-class output field so the divergence is visible rather than silent. A fallback source that is ALWAYS reachable never exercises the fallback, so the 'safe' branch never runs.
